turns.user_text: Which deep learning models were compared for lung cancer CT scan classification?
turns.answer:
Based on the retrieved research papers, several deep learning models were compared across different studies for lung cancer CT scan classification:

### Primary Experimental Comparisons
1. **Enhanced CNN vs. Pre-trained Architectures**:
   One study evaluated an **Enhanced Convolutional Neural Network (CNN)** developed from scratch against five pre-trained deep learning models [Deep learning-based approach to diagnose lung cancer using CT-scan images.pdf, p.1, p.12]:
   * **ConvNeXtSmall** (ConvNeXt) [Deep learning-based approach to diagnose lung cancer using CT-scan images.pdf, p.1, p.7]
   * **VGG16** [Deep learning-based approach to diagnose lung cancer using CT-scan images.pdf, p.1, p.7]
   * **ResNet50** [Deep learning-based approach to diagnose lung cancer using CT-scan images.pdf, p.1, p.7]
   * **InceptionV3** [Deep learning-based approach to diagnose lung cancer using CT-scan images.pdf, p.1, p.7]
   * **EfficientNetB0** [Deep learning-based approach to diagnose lung cancer using CT-scan images.pdf, p.1, p.7]

2. **Four-Model CNN Architecture Comparison**:
   Another study conducted a systematic comparative analysis of four CNN architectures for three-class CT classification (Normal, Benign, and Malignant) [AI-Powered Lung Cancer Detection- Assessing VGG16 and CNN Architectures for CT Scan Image Classification.pdf, p.11, p.25]:
   * **VGG16** [AI-Powered Lung Cancer Detection- Assessing VGG16 and CNN Architectures for CT Scan Image Classification.pdf, p.11]
   * **ResNet50** [AI-Powered Lung Cancer Detection- Assessing VGG16 and CNN Architectures for CT Scan Image Classification.pdf, p.11]
   * **MobileNetV2** [AI-Powered Lung Cancer Detection- Assessing VGG16 and CNN Architectures for CT Scan Image Classification.pdf, p.11]
   * **InceptionV3** [AI-Powered Lung Cancer Detection- Assessing VGG16 and CNN Architectures for CT Scan Image Classification.pdf, p.11]

---

### Additional Comparisons in Related Literature
* **3D CNN Models**: V et al. compared 3D CNN architectures including **AlexNet**, **CNN-T5**, and **VGG16** for classifying CT and PET scans [AI-Powered Lung Cancer Detection- Assessing VGG16 and CNN Architectures for CT Scan Image Classification.pdf, p.3].
* **Ensemble Models**: Kumaran et al. compared and integrated an ensemble combining **VGG16**, **ResNet50**, and **InceptionV3** [AI-Powered Lung Cancer Detection- Assessing VGG16 and CNN Architectures for CT Scan Image Classification.pdf, p.3].
* **Traditional vs. Deep CNNs**: Xu compared **traditional/basic CNN models** with deeper architectures like **VGG16** [AI-Powered Lung Cancer Detection- Assessing VGG16 and CNN Architectures for CT Scan Image Classification.pdf, p.3].

turns.user_text: And which of them was the most accurate?
turns.answer:
Based on the provided research papers, two studies specifically compare multiple deep learning models for lung cancer CT scan classification and report their highest accuracy achievements:

1. In the study comparing VGG16, MobileNetV2, ResNet50, and InceptionV3, **VGG16** achieved the highest test accuracy at **98.18%** [AI-Powered Lung Cancer Detection- Assessing VGG16 and CNN Architectures for CT Scan Image Classification.pdf, p. 15].
2. In another comparative evaluation of multiple models (including an Enhanced CNN, VGG16, EfficientNetB0, ResNet50, ConvNeXtSmall, and InceptionV3), an **Enhanced CNN** model achieved the highest overall performance with **100% accuracy**, while **VGG16** achieved the highest accuracy among pre-trained models at **99%** [Deep learning-based approach to diagnose lung cancer using CT-scan images.pdf, p. 14].
